resumo.en: A pitch manifesto for POVA's phone launch in Brazil, built around the country coming together for the 2026 World Cup.

desafio.en:
POVA, Tecno's phone line, was launching in Brazil in time for the 2026 World Cup, and Cappuccino was pitching for the launch. The manifesto had to sell two things at once: the campaign's big idea, a whole people coming together around the Cup, and its tone.

The material was stock footage, the kind anyone can license, plus a few AI-generated images, and there was about a week to finish. The job was to make generic images feel like they could only belong to POVA.

processo.en:
I treated the stock as raw material, not as the film. First the grade: every shot pulled into POVA's palette, so clips from different sources read as one world. On top, a layer of tech effects to give the images the brand's texture. The manifesto text moves on screen as animated type, so the idea is there to read, not just to hear.

Even with stock and AI images in the mix, the edit stays organic: a lot of movement, people dancing, cut to the beat of the track, with a Brazilian swing for a brand arriving in the country. Creative direction by Camila Teshima and Diego Araujo Torres, art direction by Cristhian Fonteles.

resultado.en: A 60-second manifesto, made in a week in 2026, that put the big idea on screen: a country united by the Cup, with the phone in every hand. The account went to another agency. The film stays here because it shows how I turn generic stock into a brand's voice on a tight deadline.
